b_actuators.json.conventions: body_h = bottom face to top of the main rectangular housing (excludes spline; any raised output boss is INCLUDED in shaft_h, which is spline top above that face). tab_z = tab UNDERSIDE above body bottom. shaft_offset = output axis to the NEARER body end (not tab end). Stall torque is the LOWEST-voltage datasheet figure (conservative); higher-voltage figure is in note.
b_actuators.json.warning: Hobby-servo clones vary by 0.3-1 mm between batches. Model tab holes as slots and body pockets with clearance; measure one physical unit before a final print, especially fields flagged UNVERIFIED in note.

_meta.policy: Every entry has a source URL that was opened and a confidence (datasheet|standard|multiple-vendors|typical). Values marked UNVERIFIED or typical in a note should be measured on the real part before printing a final version.

M1.6.note: Opened 2026-10-31. Optimas row 'M1.6 | 0.35 | 1.25 | 1.7 | 1.8 | 2' = tap drill 1.25, clearance close 1.7 / medium (normal) 1.8 / free 2.0 (clearance_hole = medium, same rule as M2). ISO 4762 socket head (Engineers Edge row 'M1.6 x 0.35 | 1.6000 | 3.0000 | 1.6000 | 1.5600'): dk 3.0, k 1.6, hex socket 1.56 (the table's 'Hex Width' column, as printed). Countersunk ISO 7046-1 (fasten.it): dk nom=max 3.0, k 1.0 (no ISO 10642 socket countersunk at M1.6). Hex nut (Engineers Edge, ASME B18.2.4.1M style 1 metric hex nut table; the ISO 4032 table itself could not be read as text): s 3.20 max / 3.02 min, m 1.30 max / 1.05 min. accu-components lists an M1.6 ISO 4762 head as D 3 +0/-0.14, H 1.6 +0/-0.14 (agrees). Pan head ISO 7045 not transcribed (no source opened). Use: Arduino Nano mounting holes are d1.8 (boards.arduino_nano).

M2.note: Clearance = ISO 273 medium(normal) series (Optimas 'Medium fit'). Head/nut = max values. ISO 10642 does not cover M2; countersunk_head_d is ISO 7046-1/ISO 14581 dk max (90 deg, k=1.2), cross-checked at https://fasten.it/en/norms/norm/din_en_iso_14581. Nut s 3.82-4.0, m 1.35-1.6.

M2.5.note: ISO 10642 does not cover M2.5; countersunk_head_d is ISO 7046-1/ISO 14581 dk max (k=1.5). Nut s 4.82-5.0, m 1.75-2.0.

M3.note: countersunk_head_d = ISO 10642 dk theoretical max (sharp-edge cone diameter, use for the 90 deg countersink cut); actual head min 5.54; k max 1.86. Nut s 5.32-5.5, m 2.15-2.4. tspi.at also confirms SHCS/nut values.

M4.note: ISO 10642 dk theoretical max 8.96, actual min 7.53, k max 2.48. Nut s 6.78-7.0, m 2.9-3.2.

M5.note: ISO 10642 dk theoretical max 11.2, actual min 9.43, k max 3.10. Nut thickness 4.7 is ISO 4032 (m 4.5-4.7); older DIN 934 M5 nut is 4.0 thick (https://www.tspi.at/diy/screwnuts.html) - spread 0.7 mm, size pockets for 4.7.

M1.6.note: Derived with the same rules as fdm_holes.M2: clearance = ISO 273 medium 1.8 + 0.1 (typical printed-hole shrink); nut_pocket_af = nut s 3.2 + 0.2 (the +0.2 mm Hubs rule cited in fdm_holes.M2; iterate per printer). NO PUBLISHED FDM SELF-TAP PILOT FOR M1.6 WAS FOUND: Bambu Lab's screw-hole guide (MakerWorld post 1182854, mirrored on forum.bambulab.com 217352) starts at M2 / BT2 and only states the rule 'keep the hole diameter equal to the pitch diameter'; no M1.6 row. self_tap_pilot is therefore deliberately omitted (note kerf.iface.screw_spec then falls back to screws.M1.6 tap_drill 1.25, a metal tap-drill size - print-test before relying on a self-tapped M1.6 in PLA/PETG; through-bolting with a nut or a heat-set insert is not catalogued either: no M1.6 insert size sourced). No heat-set insert data.

M2.note: Insert: CNC Kitchen M2 standard (D1 3.6, L 3.0, hole 3.2, wall 1.3). heatset_min_depth = L + 2 pitches (SPIROL rule). self_tap_pilot = Bambu Lab PLA table, M2 machine screw cut into a vertical (Z-axis) printed hole; horizontal hole 2.10; PETG HF vertical 1.70. clearance_hole = ISO 273 normal 2.4 + 0.1 (typical). nut_pocket_af = ISO 4032 s 4.0 + 0.2 (Hubs: +0.2 mm, 0.1 per side, iterate per printer).

M2.5.note: Insert: CNC Kitchen M2.5 standard (D1 4.6, L 4.0, hole 4.0, wall 1.6). Pilot: Bambu PLA vertical 2.30 (horizontal 2.50; PETG HF vertical 2.15). clearance 2.9+0.1 typical; nut pocket 5.0+0.2.

M3.note: Insert: CNC Kitchen M3 standard 5.7 mm (D1 4.6, centre tip 3.9, hole 4.0, wall 1.6; opened on its own product page). Alternatives: M3 short L 3.0 same hole; M3 Voron L 4.0, D1 5.0, hole 4.4, wall 1.3. Pilot: Bambu PLA vertical 2.72 (horizontal 2.90; PETG HF vertical 2.60). clearance 3.4+0.1 typical; nut pocket 5.5+0.2. self_tap_pilot is the Bambu PLA vertical value; self_tap_pilot_petg is the PETG HF vertical value from the same Bambu forum table.

M4.note: Insert: CNC Kitchen M4 standard (D1 6.3, L 8.1, hole 5.6, wall 2.1); M4 short L 4.0 same hole. Pilot: Bambu PLA vertical 3.55 (horizontal 3.75; PETG HF vertical 3.40). clearance 4.5+0.1 typical; nut pocket 7.0+0.2.

M5.note: Insert: CNC Kitchen M5 standard (D1 7.1, L 9.5, hole 6.4, wall 2.6) - datasheet grade; M5 short L 5.8 same hole. self_tap_pilot 4.45 is EXTRAPOLATED (Bambu table stops at M4; M3/M4 vertical PLA = 0.89-0.91 x d) - print a test coupon. clearance 5.5+0.1 typical; nut pocket 8.0+0.2.

shoulder_4_m3.note: Shoulder screw as a pivot: the 4 mm ground shoulder is the bearing, the M3 thread below it goes into an insert or tapped hole, and the shoulder end bottoms on the threaded part so the head never clamps the moving part. Head = McMaster low-profile slotted type (socket-head versions are 6 x 3). Thread length 4.5 (McMaster, Zoro) or 4.0 (Accu).

pin_3mm.note: ISO 8734 / DIN 6325 hardened dowel, tolerance m6. ISO 286 m6 for d<=3 mm = +0.002/+0.008 -> 3.002-3.008 (oversize). Printed press-fit hole ~2.9-3.0, slip hole ~3.1-3.2 (typical, test per printer). lengths = Bambu Lab D3 stainless dowel pin range (6-50 mm); printed hole sizes come from fdm_fits.pin.

PLA.note: Bambu PLA Basic TDS V2.0. Z modulus 2160. Poisson from measured FDM PLA at 100% infill (0.35; lit. 0.33-0.35): https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10096656

PETG.note: Bambu PETG Basic TDS V2.0 (PETG HF TDS not opened). Z modulus 1120. Bambu PETG Translucent TDS gives only 33 MPa XY. Poisson 0.38 = typical (not from TDS).

CF-PETG.note: Bambu PETG-CF TDS (V3.0 content). Z modulus 1340. Poisson typical.

PA6-CF.note: Bambu PA6-CF TDS v2; specimens annealed and dried 80C/12h (DRY values; moisture lowers strength/stiffness substantially). Z modulus 2170. Density 1.09 confirmed by https://filament2print.com/en/filaments/3669-pa6-cf-bambu-lab.html though low for CF-nylon (Sunlu PA6-CF lists 1.2). Poisson typical.

ABS.note: Bambu ABS TDS V2.0, re-opened and quoted verbatim: Young's XY 3800 +/-190, Z 2960. SUSPICIOUS: same sheet gives bending modulus XY 1880, Z 1590, and ABS is usually ~2000-2400 MPa; for FEA stiffness use ~1900-2000 (conservative). Poisson typical.

ASA.note: Bambu ASA TDS V2.0. Older Bambu ASA TDS (https://polyalkemi.no/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/Bambu_ASA_Technical_Data_Sheet.pdf) gives XY 37 / Z 31 MPa, same modulus 2450 (Z 2120); use 37 XY if conservative. Poisson typical.

TPU.note: Bambu TPU 95A TDS (not the newer 95A HF). Shore 95A. Z modulus 7.8. Elastomer: Poisson ~0.45-0.49 is typical (not from TDS); linear FEA is not valid for large strain.

cf_tube_4x2.note: Pultruded. Density 1.5 also at https://www.rockwestcomposites.com/47310-2.html (62% fibre); R&G lists ~1.78 for its pultruded rods (https://r-g.de/en/art/700006). Tolerance typically +/-0.1 OD (Easy Composites).

cf_rod_3.note: R&G lists 3.0 mm (DPP grade tol mostly -0.03/-0.1, i.e. undersize) and density ~1.78; Rock West pultruded rod 1.5 g/cm3. Consensus 1.5 used; spread 0.28 g/cm3.

MG996R.note: 2026-10-31 re-sourced from 2 TowerPro drawings, 7 independently made CAD models (measured here with build123d/trimesh; spot-checked) and 4 published mounts; no caliper measurement of a real MG996R is published. Cable boss is a KEEP-OUT envelope covering every source (location at the output end near the bottom is certain; size is not): protrusion 7.0, z 2.5-10.5 (cable_boss_z0 2.5, cable_boss_h 8.0), width 8.0. DS3218.current_note: DSSERVO DS3218MG spec table as reproduced on the AIFITLAB listing (opened 2026-10-31): operating voltage range 4.8-6.8 V; idle current (at stopped) 4 mA @5 V / 5 mA @6.8 V; stall current (at locked) 1.8 A @5 V / 2.6 A @6.8 V. stall_current_a takes the 6.8 V figure (conservative for any supply up to 6.8 V; 1.8 A applies on a 5 V rail). idle_current_a is the 6.8 V figure. running_current_a is NOT published by DSSERVO or any vendor found (servodatabase.com/servo/dsservo lists 'running current 4-5 A', which is the idle 4/5 mA mis-scaled x1000, so ignored); it is omitted so kerf/electrical.py uses stall current for running too (conservative). Only one vendor copy of the DS3218 current table was found; the rcdrone.top DSSERVO pages carry no current figures. Forum estimate (forum.arduino.cc/t/powering-12-ds3218-servos-at-once/1415585) of 1.8-2.5 A per servo is consistent.
DS3218.lead_note: DSSERVO DS3218MG spec table on the AIFITLAB listing (opened 2026-10-31): 'Connector wire 300+/-5mm' (5 V and 6.8 V columns). Connector not named there; the DS3225 table (52Pi) gives 'JR-3Pin-2.54mm'.

pca9685_adafruit.name: Adafruit 16-Channel 12-bit PWM/Servo Driver, I2C (PCA9685), product 815
pca9685_adafruit.note: Outline and holes from Adafruit's own Eagle board (rev C, opened 2026-10-31): outline x -1.905..60.325, y -6.477..18.923 = 62.23 x 25.4 mm (fab print: 2.45 in; product page '62.5 x 25.4 x 3 mm'); 4 plated MOUNTINGHOLE_2.5 (drill 2.5, pad 3.2) at (1.27, 15.748), (1.27, -3.302), (57.15, 15.748), (57.15, -3.302) = 55.88 x 19.05 mm pattern, symmetric about the board centre (29.21, 6.223). Learn guide: 'Holes are 2.5mm diameter'; M2 screws (M2.5 has no clearance). Adafruit STEP model (same frame, measured with build123d): PCB 1.57 thick; 2-pin 3.5 mm terminal block top 8.52 above the PCB top, the four 3x4 servo headers' pins 8.41 above; pins below the PCB 1.4 (headers) / 2.0 (terminal block) -> component_height 8.5, component_height_below 2.0. Servo headers sit along the -y long edge (connectors plug in from above, cables leave toward -y); terminal block at the +y edge at x = 29.21 (board centre). The 6-pin 0.1 in side headers (JP3/JP4 at the short edges) and the optional V+ electrolytic (C2) are NOT in the STEP model; if fitted, pins add ~8.5 above or below. Weight: 'no headers or terminal block: 5.5 grams', with them 9 g (product page). Voltages (learn guide pinouts): VCC logic '3 - 5V max!'; V+ servo power 'provide 5-6VDC if you are using servos', 'If you have to, you can go higher to 12VDC'; V+ 'is not used at all by the chip'. Terminal block has reverse-polarity protection (README; P-FET AOD417, Q1 in the Eagle file). current_a 0.021 = logic draw bound, derived: NXP PCA9685 datasheet Table 14 IDD max 10 mA (operating, no load, VDD 2.3-5.5 V) + power LED on VCC through 470 ohm (Eagle: LED1-R10 on VCC), bounded at 5 V/470 = 10.6 mA. pwm_current_a 0.025: per-output limit (learn guide 'Max current per pin is 25mA'; NXP 25 mA/pin, 400 mA package total) - signal lines only. NO V+ CURRENT RATING IS PUBLISHED by Adafruit (product page, learn guide, README checked), so vplus_current_a is deliberately omitted. For reference only (not a rating): Eagle traces are 0.81 mm from the terminal block to the FET (PWRIN) and 1.778 mm (some 1.016 mm segments) on the servo V+ rail; copper weight not stated. Arduino forum users warn the traces/MOSFET cannot carry many high-current servos (forum.arduino.cc/t/powering-12-ds3218-servos-at-once/1415585). With 5 stall-capable servos (up to ~13 A), feed servo V+ from the supply through a separate splice/bus and use the board only for signal + GND.
pca9685_adafruit.terminal_note: Servo plugs and the signal/GND jumpers push onto its 0.1 in male headers (3x4 servo blocks + 6-pin side headers), so wiring runs default to header ends here. The V+ 2-pin 3.5 mm terminal block is a screw terminal: set ends: {to: screw} on a run that lands there.

pin.note: Hole diameter = pin d + allowance, for a tuned Bambu printer. press: CCI (Bambu H2D) press/interference 0-0.05 mm per side -> +0.05 on diameter; a steel ISO 8734 m6 pin is +0.002..+0.008 oversize so this grips; CCI warns 0 can still be too tight. free (rotating hinge knuckle): CCI hinges 0.15-0.2 per side on Bambu, Sovol PLA slip 0.15-0.25 per side -> +0.35 on diameter. Print a test coupon on the real printer/material before the final print; looser printers (Ultimaker class) need ~+0.4 press / +0.7 free.

awg.note: PowerStream 'Max Amps for Chassis Wiring' column; diameter_mm is the bare solid-conductor diameter (stranded wire is slightly larger; insulation not included). Derate for bundles/enclosed runs (the same page's 'power transmission' column is ~4-6x lower: 12 AWG 9.3 A, 18 AWG 2.3 A, 22 AWG 0.92 A).
